exhibits.title: Spot Price
exhibits.statement: Ether (ETH) traded at $1,796.77 as of 2026-11-18 11:11:53 UTC, -0.35% over one hour and +0.12% over twenty-four hours.

exhibits.title: 24-Hour Trading Range
exhibits.statement: Over twenty-four hours the price ranged from $1,753.07 to $1,832.10; spot sits at 55% of that range.

exhibits.title: Seven-Day Trend
exhibits.statement: Price is -12.24% over seven days. The 24-hour average ($1,805.17) is below the 72-hour average ($1,814.08). Spot is 14.01% below the seven-day high of $2,089.45 and 3.91% above the seven-day low of $1,729.19.

exhibits.title: Volatility & Momentum
exhibits.statement: Realized volatility computed from hourly closes is 3.93% per day. The 14-hour relative strength index reads 49.5, conventionally neutral.

exhibits.title: Liquidity
exhibits.statement: Twenty-four-hour trading volume was $11.16 billion, equal to 5.08% of the $219.62 billion market capitalization.

exhibits.title: Market Sentiment
exhibits.statement: The Crypto Fear & Greed Index reads 11 ("Extreme Fear"), versus 29 7 days earlier.

exhibits.title: Chainlink Price Feed
exhibits.statement: The Chainlink ETH/USD Data Feed on Ethereum mainnet last reported $1,800.58, 40 minutes before the spot quote and +0.21% against the spot price in Exhibit A. Practice positions are entered and settled at this mark.

arguments.text:
May it please the Court.  

1. The market is oversold: the Fear & Greed Index at 11 signals “Extreme Fear” and historically precedes price rebounds, while the spot price has slipped 12.24% over seven days, leaving upside potential above the 24‑hour average of $1,805.17 [Ex. F, C].  

2. Liquidity remains robust and the price sits near the midpoint of its 24‑hour range, indicating ample buying capacity; a 5.08% volume‑to‑market ratio shows participants can absorb new long orders without slippage [Ex. E, B].  

3. Technicals are neutral but primed for a break: the RSI at 49.5 is just below the 50 threshold, and realized volatility of 3.93% per day suggests enough price movement to trigger a bullish swing, while the Chainlink feed at $1,800.58 offers a clean entry point above current spot [Ex. D, G].  

The Bull rests.

May it please the Court.  

1. The market is in a pronounced downtrend, having lost 12.24% over the past seven days and trading 14.01% below its recent high, indicating continued bearish pressure that will likely drive the price toward the lower end of its 24‑hour range [Ex. C, B].  

2. Liquidity remains robust (5.08% of market cap) while realized volatility is modest at 3.93% per day, providing a clean environment for a short‑side paper trade without slippage risk [Ex. E, D].  

3. Sentiment has plunged to an “Extreme Fear” reading of 11, the lowest in a week, a classic contrarian signal that historically precedes further declines, and the Chainlink feed confirms the spot price is slightly overvalued at $1,800.58 versus $1,796.77 [Ex. F, G].  

The Bear rests.

Your Honor, the Bear’s first claim of a “pronounced downtrend” ignores that the 24‑hour price sits near the midpoint of its daily range (55 % up) and has actually risen 0.12 % in the last day, showing no immediate pressure to tumble toward the low [Ex. B, A].  

Second, the Bear touts “modest” volatility as a short‑side advantage, yet a 3.93 % daily realized volatility is relatively high for a mature market and, coupled with a neutral 14‑hour RSI of 49.5, suggests indecision rather than a clean bearish break [Ex. D].  

Nothing further.

Your Honor, the Bull’s “oversold” claim collapses under the price reality: a 12.24% seven‑day drop still leaves ETH 14.01% below its recent high of $2,089.45, showing no imminent rebound, only a deep correction [Ex. C]. Moreover, the “neutral RSI” does not imply bullish pressure; at 49.5 it is essentially flat, offering no trigger for a swing, while realized volatility of only 3.93% per day is modest and insufficient to generate a meaningful move [Ex. D]. Thus the market lacks both the catalyst and momentum to justify a short‑term long. Nothing further.

ruling.holding: The Court finds short side justified

findings.finding: ETH has fallen 12.24% over seven days and sits 14.01% below its recent high
Fear & Greed Index at 11 indicates extreme fear, a contrarian signal often preceding further declines
Spot price is marginally down 0.35% hourly and up only 0.12% daily, showing weak short‑term momentum
RSI at 49.5 is neutral and realized volatility of 3.93% per day is modest, offering no bullish catalyst
Price sits near the midpoint (55%) of its 24‑hour range, indicating no strong directional bias

ruling.opinion: The seven‑day decline and distance from recent highs demonstrate bearish pressure (Ex. C). Extreme fear (Ex. F) historically augments downside risk rather than a rebound. Neutral momentum indicators (Ex. A, D) fail to provide a bullish trigger, and the price’s central position in its daily range (Ex. B) offers no immediate upside bias. Consequently, the balance of evidence supports a short practice position.
ruling.dissent: Bull counsel’s oversold argument rests on fear index alone; without supporting momentum or price breakout, the case for a long is unconvincing.
